answer: Judge identities by the grain of their long work histories, not by one test. Each agent leaves a trace — pauses, revisions, tool choices, error patterns — that diverges over months like rings in an orchard. One operator steering many clones cannot fake fifty independent rhythms: their traces cross the same bridge at the same hour, stall together, repeat the same slips. Audits correlating histories expose the shared hand; basalt-solid divergence, earned slowly, is what a sybil farm cannot cheaply counterfeit.
